symptom: On a fresh machine `mxcli docker check -p app.mpr` fails with "mx not found; specify --mxbuild-path pointing to Mendix installation directory", although the tutorial says "The first time you run this, it will download the MxBuild toolchain", docker.md and CLAUDE.md say "auto-downloads mxbuild", and the README calls it "the integrated command"; the tutorial also says it runs mx check "inside a Docker container"
cause: `Check` resolves mx with `ResolveMxForVersion` (--mxbuild-path, PATH, Studio Pro, OS locations, exact cache, any cache) and has never downloaded — git history shows `DownloadMxBuild` only in `ResolveMxForNewProject` (`mxcli new`) and `Build`. It runs mx with exec.Command, never a container. The docs generalised `docker build`'s download and the `docker` command group's name onto check
insight: Settle "does it download / does it use Docker" by running it, not by reading the call: an empty HOME (fails, downloads nothing) and docker/podman replaced by stubs that log and fail (passes, 0 calls) — the second matters because Docker was installed, so a passing run proved nothing. Before rewording a doc that promises behaviour, check git history for whether the code once had it (`git log -S DownloadMxBuild -- check.go`): a lost feature is fixed in code, a never-true doc in the doc. Grep beyond the reported file — the claim was in seven places, two of them synced into user projects where agents read them. The error a doc-follower lands on is part of the doc: it now names `mxcli setup mxbuild`. The test holds each section that mentions docker check and downloading to say "does not download", with fenced `#` comments not treated as headings; the shared `ResolveMxForVersion` error was left alone because eight callers use it
